newsitem.title: TURKEY: Turk bidders form partnership in key bank sell-off.
newsitem.headline: Turk bidders form partnership in key bank sell-off.

text.p: The best bidder in the tender for the privatisation of a Turkish government bank has formed a partnership with the third best bidder to help finance the $74-million downpayment in the sell-off, the company said.
Dogan Kumascilik, a textile producer which offered $185 million for Etibank, said the partnership was formed with Turk Cimentosu ve Kireci A.S., a private producer of cement and mortar production.
"The partnership will cover various economic investments including the purchase of Etibank, tendered by the Privatisation Administration (OIB)," Dogan Kumascilik said in a statement.
It did not give other details on the partnership.
The OIB said it had extended the deadline for the downpayment in the sale of Etibank, the government's second bank to be privatised, to June 13 from June 6.
Etibank was sold in March to Dogan Kumascilik through an open auction tender, but the company has failed to pay the 40-percent downpayment required by the sale agreement.
The remaining portion will have to be paid in two years with a 10 percent annual interest rate, which brings the total price tag to $210 million.

Officials earlier said the deadline would not be extended for a second time and the High Board of Privatisation, the top decision making body chaired by Prime Minister Necmettin Erbakan, would now decide on the sell-off of Etibank.
The board has the authority to award the tender to the second or the third bidder or start a new sell-off.
The government privatised Sumerbank, the first bank to be sold-off, for $103.5 million to a textiles and brewer company in 1995.
